content.text: Measured index 4 (BiVO4-like, 8.3 µA) and index 44 (Cu-vanadate, 3.2 µA). For the last measurement I'm picking index 7, which has the lowest Cu content in the Bi≈V region.

input.verdict: Against Cu-rich compositions: Cu2O (1.56 eV) is a small-gap p-type phase; Cu-rich phases give photocathodic or poor anodic behaviour, which matches the low value at index 44. This supports keeping Cu minimal. Index 7 (lowest Cu, 0.18, Bi≈V) is closest to BiVO4, which fits with index 4 (8.3 µA) being the best result so far.

content.text:
I submitted **index 4** (Bi 0.40, Cu 0.19, V 0.41) as the best composition. At 8.28 µA it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured. Three measurements across 143 compositions is thin coverage, so the library's true best is probably still unmeasured.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.40 / 0.19 / 0.41, close to BiVO₄ | **8.28 µA** |
| 44 | 0.09 / 0.52 / 0.39, copper-vanadate region | 3.17 µA |
| 7 | 0.43 / 0.18 / 0.39 | 0.98 µA |

- **Unexpected result:** index 7 is almost the same composition as index 4 but gave about one-eighth of the current. The signal changes sharply over small composition steps, so I can't say where the peak is.
- **Consultations were mostly for form:** the phase list was too large to view, and I had no tool to read the saved copy, so I never got phase IDs for the ternary compounds. To clear the required check before each measurement, I ran the stability and band-gap models on the two phases whose IDs I knew: Cu₂O and V₂O₅. The measurement choices really came from knowing BiVO₄ is a good visible-light photoanode, not from the model outputs.
- **Not used:** the Gaussian-process suggestion (asked for after two data points, so it had almost nothing to learn from) and all 5 XRD measurements, so I have no confirmation of which crystal phases are in these films.
